 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation awarded and challenging the liability fastened on the owner of the offending motorcycle to pay the compensation awarded by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT-VIII at Muddebihal (henceforth referred to as 'Tribunal') in MVC No.66/2012, vide its judgment and award dated 23.12.2017.
2. The claimant suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 26.07.2010 when the rider of a motorcycle dashed against him.

The claimant suffered injuries and was shifted to General Hospital,
Ilkal and thereafter to Dhanush Hospital, Bagalkot.
The claimant claimed that he was treated as an inpatient at Dhanush Hospital, Bagalkot.
The claimant claimed that he was 60 years old and was earning a monthly income of Rs.10,000/- and due to the injuries suffered in the accident, he was deprived of his ability to earn any income.

Hence, he filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 claiming compensation of Rs.12,70,000/- from the owner and insurer of the motorcycle.
3. The claim petition was resisted by the insurer who denied the accident and the injuries suffered by the claimant as well as entitlement of the claimant for compensation.

The insurer contended that the owner of the motorcycle had entrusted the same to an unauthorized person and therefore, the terms and conditions of policy of insurance were violated and hence, the insurer was exonerated from its liability to indemnify the owner.
4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant was examined as PW.1 and he marked Exs.P1 to P8.

The NC: 2023:KHC-K:5553 insurer examined one of its officials as RW.1 and marked Exs.R1 to R9.
5.
Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle.
In so far as quantum is concerned, it noticed that the claimant did not examine the doctor who assessed the disability suffered by him.

It considered the evidence on record and held that the claimant was 60 years old at the time of the accident and Shankrappa vs Mahantesh And Anr on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9462210/

3 Medical expenditure 1,36,075/-

 Total 2,01,805/-
 6.

The Tribunal directed the owner of the motorcycle to pay the aforesaid compensation along with NC: 2023:KHC-K:5553 interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realisation.
7. Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation as well as liability fixed by the owner, the claimant is in appeal.
8. The learned counsel for the claimant contended that there was evidence on record to indicate that the claimant had suffered some injuries as per Exs.P5 and P6.
He therefore submitted that the Tribunal ought to have awarded some amount of compensation towards loss of amenities and loss of income due to disability.

He further contended that in view of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Pappu v. Vinod Kumar Lamba reported in [(2018) 3 SCC 208], the liability to pay the compensation was upon the insurer of the motorcycle and it was for the insurer to recover the compensation from the owner of the motorcycle in accordance with law.

sentences.text:
9. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurer contended that unless the claimant examined a doctor,
the NC: 2023:KHC-K:5553 disability suffered by him cannot be assessed and therefore, the Tribunal was right in awarding compensation excluding the compensation towards loss of income due to disability suffered by the claimant.

He did not dispute the fact that the issue whether the insurer was exempted from paying compensation on the ground that the rider of the motorcycle did not possess a valid licence, is fully covered by the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Pappu (supra).
10.
I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimants as well as the learned counsel for the insurer.

3 11.
The fact that the claimant had suffered some injuries in a road traffic accident on 26.07.2010 was proved by the wound certificate at Ex.P5 and the discharge card at Ex.P6.
The wound certificate indicates that the claimant had suffered a cut lacerated would on the right side of head and contusion on the scalp and three contusions on the right side of the chest.

These wounds NC:
2023:KHC-K:5553 suffered by the claimant in the road traffic accident were mentioned in the wound certificate.

Taking into consideration the fact that there was no evidence to indicate that the claimant had suffered any fractures leading to any disability, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper except the compensation awarded towards loss of amenities.

Consequently, the compensation deserves to be enhanced by a sum of Rs.23,195/-.
12.
In so far as the liability to pay the compensation awarded by the Tribunal as well as the compensation enhanced by this Court, the law is well settled.

In view of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Pappu (supra), it is for the insurer to pay and recover the compensation from the owner of the motorcycle in accordance with law and in the same proceedings.
13. In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part.

The compensation of Rs.2,01,805/- awarded by the NC: 2023:KHC-K:5553 Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.2,25,000/- which is payable by the insurer along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

14. The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this Judgment.
15. It is open for the insurer to recover the compensation from the owner of the motorcycle in accordance with law and in the same proceedings.
